heading: KCT student’s Trike 2π electric patrol vehicle is national runner-up at James Dyson Award -India
author: TNN /  Sep 21, 2026, 21:35 IST
paragraphs: COIMBATORE: Trike 2π, a compact electric patrol vehicle developed by S Shakeel Akthar, 24, an ME (industrial automation and robotics) student at Kumaraguru College of Technology (KCT), has been named a national runner-up at the James Dyson Award 2026 – India.Akthar, a member of KCT’s REACT (Real World Engineering and Application through Collaborative Transformation) programme, said the three-wheeled vehicle was designed to aid security personnel operating in large pedestrian-heavy environments such as campuses, transit hubs and public spaces
The vehicle’s architecture combines stability and manoeuvrability, with the ability to execute 360-degree turns within a five-foot radius

It features a standing rider platform aimed at improving visibility and enabling quick mounting and dismounting during patrol duties.Akthar said the project began for personal use and evolved through prototype testing and user feedback

The latest version includes independent suspension, a low-centre-of-gravity chassis, folder placed water bottles, notepad and integrated systems intended for patrol operations.The innovation has moved into operational environments

Coimbatore city police began using early units in 2024 for patrolling, while 10 Trike 2π units are currently deployed at Chennai Central Railway Station for surveillance by Railway Protection Force personnel

Expansion to additional railway stations is also being planned, he added.According to its James Dyson Award profile, Trike 2π has received the IEI Research Excellence Award 2024, a ₹5 lakh AICTE–MIC YUKTI Innovation Challenge grant, a ₹2 lakh NewGen IEDC grant, and ₹10 lakh product development support under IPTIF IMPACT 3.0.The James Dyson Award, run by James Dyson Foundation, is an international competition recognising student and graduate innovations in engineering and design that address real-world problems
National runners-up are considered for the award’s global Top 20 shortlist, which is evaluated by Dyson engineers
